newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann, Daimler unit form networking venture.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann, Daimler unit form networking venture.

text.p: German publishing giant Bertelsmann AG and the services division of Daimler-Benz AG said on Wednesday they had agreed to form a network services venture.
Under the agreement Daimler-Benz Interservices AG (Debis) would take a 50 percent stake in Bertelsmann's subsidiary Media-Ways, the companies said in a statement.
Debis unit Debis Systemhaus GmbH would aquire the stake in Media-Ways, which is the company that provides dial-up access to America Online in Germany.

Bertelsmann and America Online jointly operate the European commercial online service AOL, which currently has more than 200,000 subscribers. America Online has over six million subscribers worldwide.

Bertelsmann has said in the past that it wants to use the national access network it built for AOL to offer networking services to other companies, particularly for Intranets, or internal company networks based on Internet technology.

Media-Ways expects sales of 40 million marks this year and operates an Internet access network with 60 dial-up points, making it one of the largest Internet access networks in Germany, the companies said.
Initially the venture with Debis Systemhaus will have annual telecommunications revenue of around 300 million marks.
